    Why Cold Email? 5/16

    Why Cold Email?

    One of the smartest moves a B2B business can make

    Cold email is arguably the most intelligent marketing move a B2B business can make.


    Why? Because it sets up your sales process for success - before the conversation even starts.


    When you deliver genuine value upfront, you're not just booking meetings - you're building trust. You're showing the prospect that you understand their challenges and that you already have the answers they need.


    And that trust? That's your unfair advantage.


    When done right, cold email doesn't just generate leads - it builds trust and primes the close.


    Compared to other channels:


  • Paid ads - you pay for every click, even irrelevant ones
  • Content and SEO - long time to results, dependent on algorithms
  • Cold calls - highly effective, but hard to scale

    • With cold email, you're in full control: who sees your message, when, and with what angle.

    Prerequisites 6/16

    Prerequisites

    What you need before you start

    You don't need everything in your business perfectly sorted before starting cold email.


    It's actually one of the best ways to test demand, discover what your audience really needs, and start conversations that can lead to sales.


    But - let's be honest. Most people feel a bit lost the first time.


    Before you start, make sure you have:


  • A clear offer - you know exactly what you're selling and what value you bring
  • A defined ICP - you know who you're selling to: industry, company size, decision-maker role
  • Proven results - you know the story you'll tell: a case study, numbers, an outcome
  • Basic infrastructure - a domain, a website (even a simple one), and a business email address

    • If your ICP isn't fully clear yet, don't stop. Cold email in practice is one of the best ways to discover who responds and sharpen your targeting as you go.

    Mistake 1 - Validation 8/16

    Not Verifying Emails Before Sending

    The problem that kills domains silently

    Imagine you set up a campaign, wrote copy you're proud of, configured all your sequences - then hit send to a list of 500 contacts.


    48 hours later, bounce rate is sitting at 8%. Your domain starts getting negative signals. Two weeks later - you're in everyone's spam.


    This is exactly what happens when you don't verify emails before sending.


    The Common Mistake


    People buy a list, export from Apollo, import into Smartlead - and send. Without one critical step: email validation. Even in Apollo there are outdated emails. Databases go stale - that's just reality.


    Bounce rate is the speedometer of your domain's health.


  • Bounce rate below 3% - safe to send
  • Bounce rate above 3% - red alert
  • Bounce rate above 5% - ISPs start pushing you to spam

    • Once a domain gets a bad reputation, it's nearly impossible to recover. The fastest way to burn a new domain you spent two weeks warming up - is to send to an unvalidated list.


    How to Do It Right


    Before every campaign, validate your list. Always. No exceptions.


    ZeroBounce returns every address with one of these statuses:


  • VALID - send
  • INVALID - delete
  • RISKY - usually delete
  • UNKNOWN - cannot verify

    • The simple rule: send only to VALID. This can shrink your list by 10-30% - and that's completely fine. A clean list of 350 beats a list of 500 that sends you to spam.

    Mistake 2 - Too Many Inboxes 9/16

    Buying Too Many Inboxes Per Domain

    More inboxes = more damage

    The logic sounds reasonable: if I have 10 inboxes on the same domain, I can send 10x more emails.


    The problem is Google and Microsoft aren't stupid.


    The Common Mistake


    Most people new to cold email buy one domain and put 6, 8, sometimes even 12 inboxes on it. That's exactly the pattern ISPs are looking for.


    When there are too many inboxes on the same domain, it triggers a red flag. The entire domain is at risk - it's not just one inbox that gets blocked, the whole domain can take a reputation hit.


    Links between domains are also a problem. If you bought 5 domains and they all point to the same main website - Google and Microsoft identify the network and burn it together.


    The limits you should not exceed:


  • Google Workspace: up to 4 inboxes per domain
  • Microsoft 365: up to 10 inboxes, but Google is far stricter

    • How to Do It Right


    Zapmail lets you buy domains and set up Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 inboxes in one fast process, without manually touching DNS.


    After purchase, Smartlead manages rotation between inboxes and ensures you stay within limits.


    The correct formula for calculating volume:


    If you want to send 500 emails per day with Google Workspace:

  • 15 emails/day per inbox
  • 4 inboxes per domain = 60 emails/day per domain
  • 500 / 60 = ~9 domains

    • That's the right number. Not one big infrastructure - several small, clean domains.

    Mistake 3 - Warmup 10/16

    Not Warming Up Your Inboxes

    You can't send from a new inbox tomorrow

    A new inbox is like an employee who joined the company yesterday. It's unknown, has no history, and ISPs look at it with suspicion.


    If you start sending cold emails immediately - you're going straight to spam.


    The Common Mistake


    Most people buy a domain, configure DNS, and send directly to their list. The inbox itself has no reputation, even if it's Gmail.


    Email providers look at the activity history of every inbox:


  • Are there two-way conversations?
  • Are people replying?
  • Is a new inbox suddenly sending 50 emails a day to people who don't know it?

    • That last pattern is exactly what anti-spam algorithms are looking for.


    How to Do It Right


    Warmup is a process of at least two weeks where the inbox sends and receives emails gradually to build reputation.


    The rules:


  • Minimum 2 weeks of warmup before sending - 4 weeks is ideal
  • Don't send until the warmup score hits 90% or above
  • Don't stop warmup when you start sending - keep both running in parallel

    • Smartlead includes built-in automatic warmup that gradually increases volume, simulates real conversations, and gives each inbox a health score.


    Advanced tip: Run each domain for 2 weeks, let it rest for 2 weeks. This significantly extends inbox lifespan. Never warm up via manual SMTP - use a dedicated tool.

    Mistake 4 - Send Volume 11/16

    Sending Too Many Emails Per Day

    The hard caps most people ignore

    This is one of the things people resist the most - because it feels like an unnecessary limitation. But these numbers aren't a recommendation. They're hard limits set by Google and Microsoft.


    The Common Mistake


    "I have 3 Gmail inboxes - I'll send 50 emails a day from each one."


    The official cold email sending limits:


  • Google Workspace: 15 emails per day per inbox
  • Microsoft 365: 5 emails per day per inbox

    • If you exceed these limits - your inbox gets a negative reputation and you're on your way to spam.


    Microsoft is stricter. 5 emails a day is low - but that's precisely why Microsoft inboxes have higher deliverability. Google gives a bit more room - 15 per inbox - but it's far more aggressive with pattern detection.


    The practical rule:


    Google Workspace: 15 emails/day per inbox, 4 inboxes per domain = 60 emails/domain/day

    Microsoft 365: 5 emails/day per inbox, 10 inboxes per domain = 50 emails/domain/day


    How to Do It Right


    Stick to the limits - and compensate by adding more inboxes and domains, not by pushing the boundaries.


    Want to send 300 emails per day?

  • With Google: 5 domains, 4 inboxes each = 300 emails
  • With Microsoft: 6 domains, 10 inboxes each = 300 emails

    • Advanced tip: Spread across both Google and Microsoft. Don't put everything on one provider.


    Smartlead automatically caps sends according to the hard limits, spreads sending throughout the day, and manages rotation between inboxes.

    Mistake 5 - Monitoring 12/16

    Not Monitoring Inbox Health

    Inboxes degrade - it's not a question of 'if', it's a question of 'when'

    Even if you did everything right - validated emails, warmed up the inbox, stayed within limits - inboxes degrade over time.


    Every email sent, every bounce, every spam report - they all accumulate and affect inbox reputation. Monitoring is what separates a campaign that keeps producing results from one that slowly dies.


    The Common Mistake


    You configure a campaign, launch it - and don't touch it for weeks. Meanwhile, one inbox is deteriorating. The warmup score dropped to 70%. Bounce rate climbed to 4%. And results start declining - but slowly enough that nobody notices.


    When these indicators go red - it's time to act:


  • Warmup score drops below 90% - weak inbox, replace it
  • Bounce rate exceeds 3% (with 1,000+ sends) - list problem or inbox problem
  • Reply rate drops below 0.3% (including out-of-office) - if you're not even getting OOO replies, you're in spam

    • People wait too long. They see reply rate drop and try to fix the copy. But the problem isn't the copy - the problem is the inbox.


    How to Do It Right


    Weekly check of:


    1. Warmup score for every inbox - replace any inbox below 90%

    2. Bounce rate per campaign - above 3%? Stop and clean the list

    3. Reply rate including OOO - below 0.3%? Check deliverability before touching copy

    4. Spam reports - zero tolerance


    When an inbox falls below threshold - replace it immediately. Don't try to fix it. Just prepare a new inbox, warm it for two weeks, and swap it in.


    Smartlead shows a central dashboard with every inbox's health, warmup score, and bounce rate, and alerts you automatically to problems.

    Mistake 6 - Spintax 13/16

    Not Using Spintax

    500 identical emails = 500 emails going to spam

    Email providers like Google and Microsoft use pattern detection - they identify identical emails being sent from the same inbox to many people. When they detect the same pattern - they push you to spam.


    The Common Mistake


    You write one email template and send it identically to 200 people. Each of them receives the same email. Google sees 200 identical emails from the same address - that's exactly what's called bulk sending.


    What Spintax Is and How It Works


    Spintax lets you automatically generate different variations of the same message, so each email looks slightly different from the last.


    The syntax: {Hello|Hi|Hey} [First Name]


    When the email is sent, it randomly becomes: Hello / Hi / Hey.


    Example:


    {Hello|Hi} [Name], {I noticed|I saw|I came across} that your company {is growing fast|is expanding}. {I wanted to share|I thought you'd find it interesting} - we've worked with similar companies and {helped them|seen improvement} in [result]. {Worth a chat?|Would love to connect.}


    From a template like this you can generate hundreds of different combinations.


    Why this matters so much:


  • Looks more human - emails with small variations read as less bot-like
  • Free A/B testing - you're effectively testing multiple versions simultaneously
  • Long-term protection - the longer campaigns run, the more sensitive pattern detection becomes

    • How much spintax do you need? At least 3-4 variations for the opening sentence, 2-3 for all other elements.


    Smartlead supports spintax directly inside the sequence editor, with a preview that shows how each variation will look before sending.

    Mistake 7 - DNS 14/16

    Not Configuring DNS Correctly

    Your identity card in email infrastructure

    DNS is your identity card in email infrastructure. Without SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured correctly, ISPs can't verify that the email was actually sent by you - and you go straight to spam.


    The Common Mistake


    You set up a new inbox, hit send - and completely forget about DNS. Or worse - you try to configure DNS manually, make an error you don't catch until the campaign is already running.


    Every incorrect DNS record significantly hurts deliverability:


  • SPF not configured - receiving servers can't verify sender identity
  • DKIM missing - the email appears as "unsigned" and gets a low score
  • DMARC absent - no protection, ISPs don't trust you

    • And you won't know there's a problem until reply rate collapses.


    How to Do It Right


    Zapmail automatically configures SPF, DKIM, and DMARC at the time of domain purchase. You don't need to touch DNS manually. The tool does it for you.


    If you're configuring manually, here's what must be in place:


  • SPF - defines who is authorized to send on behalf of your domain
  • DKIM - adds a digital signature to every email
  • DMARC - defines what to do with emails that fail SPF/DKIM

    • After configuring, always verify with MXToolbox that everything is set correctly before you start sending.

    Mistake 8 - HTML 15/16

    Sending HTML Emails

    Designed emails look professional - and land in spam

    HTML emails look professional. Logo, colors, buttons, images. Just like a newsletter.


    The problem? That's exactly what ISPs are looking for to identify mass marketing - and push you to spam.


    The Common Mistake


    Sending cold email with a styled HTML template - logo at the top, CTA button, design tables. It looks professional, but to spam detection algorithms it looks exactly like a broadcast email list.


    Every HTML element adds spam points:


  • Logo and images - flags the email as promotional
  • Tracking links - triggers red flags
  • HTML tables - same pattern as mass newsletters
  • Styled CTA button - no human sends that to a friend

    • Cold email = plain text. Always.


    Think about how you write an email to a friend. Plain text, short lines, no design. That's exactly what cold outreach looks like.


    The rules:


  • No logo - not in the email body, not in the signature
  • No images - not even a respectable one
  • No tracking pixels - Google Analytics, Clearbit - keep them out of cold email
  • Links - minimum. One link maximum in the entire email
  • No CTA buttons - plain text: "Worth a chat?"
  • Simple signature - name, title, phone. That's it

    • Smartlead makes it easy to send plain text sequences with all the right settings.
